label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 20

hints.title: Use the heights on the graph
hints.body: Let u=f(x). Read the lowest and highest possible values of u from the graph. Then replace f(x) by u in the expression you are asked about.
hints.recap: The graph tells you which values <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> can take.
hints.pitfall: Use the vertical values on the graph, not the horizontal coordinates where they occur.
hints.pause: Write the new quadratic and the allowed range of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: The graph tells you which values <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> can take.

hints.title: Find the highest and lowest values
hints.body: Complete the square and sketch your new quadratic over the allowed input range. Mark its two endpoints and its vertex if permitted, then compare their heights.
hints.recap: The highest or lowest value may occur at an end of the range.
hints.pitfall: The vertex gives only one of the two values you need.
hints.pause: Find the maximum and minimum, then subtract.

recall.reminder: The highest or lowest value may occur at an end of the range.

solution:
1. Use the inner range. The continuous plotted function takes every value in [−2,2]. Put u=f(x), so the target becomes g(u)=u2−u on that closed interval.

2. Find the minimum. g(u)=(u−1/2)2−1/4. Its vertex input u=1/2 is attainable, giving the minimum −1/4.

3. Compare the endpoints for the maximum. g(−2)=6 and g(2)=2, so the maximum is 6. The required difference is 6−(−1/4)=25/4. Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Optimise a quadratic over the attained output range of a plotted function
